items.prompt: My sister ___ in a hospital in Valencia.

explanation.en: A permanent situation with she needs the present simple with -s.
explanation.es: Con she, el present simple lleva -s: works.

optionNotes.en: Work has no -s, so it does not agree with my sister.
Working alone is not a full verb; it needs is.

items.prompt: A: ___ you go to the gym on Saturdays? B: No, I usually stay at home.

explanation.en: A question about a habit with you starts with do.
explanation.es: Para preguntar por un hábito con you se usa do.

optionNotes.en: Does is used with he, she and it, not with you.
Are would need an -ing form: Are you going…?

items.prompt: The bus to the airport ___ at half past six every morning.

explanation.en: The bus is it, so the verb takes -s. Every morning shows a regular event.

optionNotes.en: Leave has no -s, so it does not agree with the bus.
Leaving cannot be the only verb in the sentence.

items.prompt: He doesn't ___ coffee in the evening because he can't sleep afterwards.

explanation.en: After doesn't the main verb stays in the base form.
explanation.es: Tras doesn't, el verbo va sin -s: drink.

optionNotes.en: The -s is already in doesn't, so it is not repeated.
Doesn't is not followed by an -ing form.

items.prompt: How often ___ your brother call you?

explanation.en: Your brother is he, so the question needs does + base verb.

optionNotes.en: Do is for I, you, we and they, not for one brother.
Is would be followed by an -ing form, not by call.

items.prompt: Sofia ___ to work by train because she doesn't have a car.

explanation.en: Verbs ending in -o add -es with he, she and it: goes.
explanation.es: Los verbos acabados en -o añaden -es: goes.

optionNotes.en: Going needs is before it: Sofia is going to work. Here we talk about a habit.
optionNotes.es: Going necesita is delante. Aquí se habla de una costumbre.

optionNotes.en: Go has no -s, so it does not agree with Sofia.
